records.title: Introduction to Criminal Justice
records.header: T CRIM 101 Introduction to Criminal Justice (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 101 Introduction to Criminal Justice (5) SSc Examines the history, structure, operations, and problems with the American criminal justice system. Analyzes general and specific topics associated with the contemporary criminal justice system in order to develop a critical perspective on the nature of justice and society's response to criminal behavior.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Media, Crime, and Justice
records.header: T CRIM 155 Media, Crime, and Justice (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 155 Media, Crime, and Justice (5) SSc Investigates interrelationships between crime, justice, and media. Explores representations of crime, systems-impacted individuals, victims, and criminal legal systems as portrayed by various forms of media. Considers the impacts of these portrayals on individuals and the larger culture. Examines how media inform and filter understandings of crime and justice.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: War on Drugs: Crime and Justice
records.header: T CRIM 156 War on Drugs: Crime and Justice (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 156 War on Drugs: Crime and Justice (5) SSc Investigates how policymaking, policing, legal, and carceral agencies articulate and execute the U.S. War on Drugs. Critically analyzes prohibition and enforcement, and examines the relationship between policy, mass incarceration, and inequality. Explores changing perspectives on and approaches to prohibition.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Miscarriages of Justice
records.header: T CRIM 157 Miscarriages of Justice (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 157 Miscarriages of Justice (5) SSc Explores various types of miscarriages of justice in U.S. criminal legal systems, with significant focus on case studies of the wrongfully convicted and exonerated. Examines research conducted on the causes of wrongful convictions including eyewitness misidentification, flawed forensics, forced confessions, prosecutorial misconduct, ineffective assistance of counsel, and others.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: U.S. Hate Crime and Organized Hate
records.header: T CRIM 158 U.S. Hate Crime and Organized Hate (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 158 U.S. Hate Crime and Organized Hate (5) SSc Explores definitions and causes of bias-motivated crime in the U.S. and the individual, community, and social consequences of hate crime. Critically analyzes ideologies, recruitment, subcultures, tactics, and activities of organized hate movements, and examines formal legal and collective social efforts to confront hate crime and organized hate groups.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Cybercrime and Social Justice
records.header: T CRIM 211 Cybercrime and Social Justice (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 211 Cybercrime and Social Justice (5) SSc Explores cybercrime through a social justice framework, evaluating how digital crimes disproportionately impact various groups and intersect with existing inequalities. Examines relationships between technology, law enforcement, and justice. Students will analyze approaches to cyber threats while considering equity, privacy, constitutional rights, and fairness in digital spaces.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: School Safety and Violence Prevention
records.header: T CRIM 212 School Safety and Violence Prevention (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 212 School Safety and Violence Prevention (5) SSc Examines the causes, consequences, and prevention of violence in school settings. Explores key theoretical frameworks, policies, practices, and ongoing issues associated with creating safe learning environments. Topics include security and surveillance, school discipline, restorative practices, behavioral threat assessment, mental health supports, bullying, and school shootings.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Diversity and Social Justice in Criminology
records.header: T CRIM 225 Diversity and Social Justice in Criminology (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: T CRIM 225 Diversity and Social Justice in Criminology (5) SSc, DIV Explores definitions and implications of diversity and social justice theory. Applies principles of social justice to criminal justice contexts within the United States. Analyzes social positons in relation to relative privilege and power. Emphasizes experiential and reflective learning.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Introduction to the Sociology of Deviance and Social Control
records.header: T CRIM 271 Introduction to the Sociology of Deviance and Social Control (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 271 Introduction to the Sociology of Deviance and Social Control (5) SSc Examines social constructions of norms and deviance, processes used to control deviance, the impact of societal responses to deviance, and cross-cultural variations. Analyzes why some behaviors, differences, and people are considered deviant while others are not. Discusses formal and informal responses to deviance including stigmatization, criminalization, and medicalization. Course equivalent to: SOC 271.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Restorative Justice
records.header: T CRIM 272 Restorative Justice (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 272 Restorative Justice (5) SSc Explores the philosophical underpinnings of restorative justice (RJ) and its application in the context of harm-doing, both inside and outside of criminal legal systems. Analyzes the effectiveness, risks, and benefits of RJ practice for RJ stakeholders. Explores the potential to facilitate systems change.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: White Collar Crime
records.header: T CRIM 275 White Collar Crime (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 275 White Collar Crime (5) SSc Examines harms committed by states, agencies, corporations, and those in white-collar occupations. Explores social definitions, causes, and consequences of these offenses. Critically examines the social contexts that promote such violations, and explores social, legal, and community responses to white collar criminality.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Mass Shootings in the United States
records.header: T CRIM 276 Mass Shootings in the United States (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 276 Mass Shootings in the United States (5) SSc Examines the causes and prevention of mass shootings in the United States. Analyzes social, cultural, psychological, and political factors that contribute to this phenomenon, and the impact of these events on individuals, communities, and society. Explores historical context, motivations, current trends, media coverage, legal and policy issues, and potential solutions.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Settler Colonial Crimes Throughout U.S. History
records.header: T CRIM 277 Settler Colonial Crimes Throughout U.S. History (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 277 Settler Colonial Crimes Throughout U.S. History (5) SSc Explores the range of settler colonial crimes committed against Indigenous peoples throughout the U.S. and its territories. Analyzes the doctrines and ideologies enabling crimes. Examines damage through the perspectives of law, human rights, and social harm. Analyzes Indigenous philosophies and practices of resistance.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Women, Crime, and Justice
records.header: T CRIM 352 Women, Crime, and Justice (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 352 Women, Crime, and Justice (5) SSc Explores the history, societal impact, and future of women within U.S. criminal legal systems. Focuses on factors that contribute to the involvement of women in the criminal legal system, including poverty, trauma, substance use, and major mental illness. The course explores promising and proven gender-responsive approaches for working with system-involved women.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Juvenile Delinquency and Society
records.header: T CRIM 360 Juvenile Delinquency and Society (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 360 Juvenile Delinquency and Society (5) SSc Critically examines conceptions of youthful delinquency, looking at its causes, as well as the responses of the juvenile legal system. Analyzes historical and contemporary perspectives on delinquent behavior and explores current trends in juvenile legal system policy and practice, including prevention and intervention efforts.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Mental Health, Substance Use and the Criminal Justice System
records.header: T CRIM 361 Mental Health, Substance Use and the Criminal Justice System (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 361 Mental Health, Substance Use and the Criminal Justice System (5) SSc Examines the intersection of mental health, substance use, and the criminal justice system. Focuses on the interaction of mental health and criminal justice practice. Explores the prevalence of mental health and substance use and best practices for treatment. Offered: jointly with TSOCWF 361.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Criminological Theory
records.header: T CRIM 362 Criminological Theory (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 362 Criminological Theory (5) SSc Surveys the major schools of thought related to the causes of crime and criminalization, positions theories in their historical contexts, and discusses each perspective's assumptions about human nature. Outlines current debates and critiques of various schools of thought and explores the policy implications of each theoretical perspective.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: The Criminalization of Immigration
records.header: T CRIM 363 The Criminalization of Immigration (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: T CRIM 363 The Criminalization of Immigration (5) SSc, DIV Examines the criminalization of immigration in the United States and globally and the ways in which social institutions have implemented immigration policies. Analyzes the unintended consequences of criminalizing policies and practices. Explores psychosocial effects on the lives of diverse immigrants, their families, and ethnic minority communities. Offered: jointly with TSOCWF 363.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: LGBTQ+ Persons, Crime, and Justice
records.header: T CRIM 364 LGBTQ+ Persons, Crime, and Justice (5) SSc, DIV
records.text: T CRIM 364 LGBTQ+ Persons, Crime, and Justice (5) SSc, DIV Examines experiences of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer (LGBTQ+) persons across criminal legal systems, the criminalization of queerness, and the historical impacts of policy and law. Scrutinizes discriminatory systems practices toward LGBTQ+ people with intersecting identities (race, class, gender, ability). Explores contemporary issues through critical theory and reflexivity.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Facing Harm: Victim Offender Dialogue
records.header: T CRIM 365 Facing Harm: Victim Offender Dialogue (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 365 Facing Harm: Victim Offender Dialogue (5) SSc Examines the relationship between restorative justice theory and practice. Develops skills in facilitating several models of victim offender dialogue (VOD). Articulates the benefits and risks of VOD for justice stakeholders. Critically examines the effectiveness of VOD as a response to crime and violence. Cultivates a practitioner identity.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Police and Society
records.header: T CRIM 370 Police and Society (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 370 Police and Society (5) SSc Examines the role of police within society through a social justice lens, emphasizing history, public perceptions, administration, organizational culture, and ethics. Examines contemporary concerns and controversies within law enforcement, such as use of force and issues of inequality. Surveys emerging practices in policing and examines alternative models for fostering safety.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Interpersonal Skills for the Justice Practitioner
records.header: T CRIM 371 Interpersonal Skills for the Justice Practitioner (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 371 Interpersonal Skills for the Justice Practitioner (5) SSc Focuses on skills needed to establish relationships with systems-involved individuals, including victims, and understand their experiences within a wider social context. Develops skills in interpersonal communications, empathic and collaborative relationship-building, cultural humility, and values-based practice. Explores current models of individual and systemic change. Cultivates a holistic practitioner identity. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 2.0 in T CRIM 225.

records.title: Punishment, Incarceration, and Society
records.header: T CRIM 372 Punishment, Incarceration, and Society (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 372 Punishment, Incarceration, and Society (5) SSc Focuses on the history, structure, and role of punishment and incarceration in society. Explores different theoretical justifications for punishment. Examines various practice and policy issues relevant to contemporary punishment and incarceration, including impacts on system-involved individuals, victims, and communities.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Criminal Evidence and Investigation
records.header: T CRIM 373 Criminal Evidence and Investigation (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 373 Criminal Evidence and Investigation (5) SSc Examines crime detection, techniques for case management and documentation, the concept of proof, the impact of emergent technology on the investigative process, interacting with victims and witnesses, and interviewing suspects. Emphasizes the issues that arise during the investigation of crimes such as homicides, sex offences, child abuse, and hate crimes.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Human Trafficking
records.header: T CRIM 374 Human Trafficking (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 374 Human Trafficking (5) SSc Examines domestic and international human trafficking, recruitment, and control methodologies. Considers labor and sexual exploitation and examines existing laws and services to combat trafficking. Analyzes the role of demand in perpetuating trafficking and the victims' trauma. Applies best practice solutions. Offered: jointly with TSOCWF 374.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Men, Masculinities, Crime, and Justice
records.header: T CRIM 375 Men, Masculinities, Crime, and Justice (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 375 Men, Masculinities, Crime, and Justice (5) SSc Explores issues related to men and masculinities in the criminal legal system. Examines the various conceptions of masculinities that increase the risks of criminality and how men "perform" masculinities within criminal legal systems.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Harm Reduction
records.header: T CRIM 376 Harm Reduction (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 376 Harm Reduction (5) SSc Examines the history and development of harm reduction approaches to drug use, sex work, and other related issues, and how these strategies can reduce harms and further complications for individuals and communities. Identifies controversies, successes, and challenges and analyses examples of innovative harm reduction policies, practices, and services. Offered: jointly with TSOCWF 376.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Reentry Success: Exploring Experiences and Programs for Returning People
records.header: T CRIM 377 Reentry Success: Exploring Experiences and Programs for Returning People (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 377 Reentry Success: Exploring Experiences and Programs for Returning People (5) SSc Examines the numerous challenges to successful reentry and integration into the community, after serving sentences in carceral facilities. Provides in-depth exploration of the issues impacting the reentry of returning people. Explores possible solutions to create successful reentry processes and outcomes. Offered: jointly with TSOCWF 377.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Criminological Research Methods
records.header: T CRIM 390 Criminological Research Methods (5)
records.text: T CRIM 390 Criminological Research Methods (5) Introduces criminological research methods, including the processes of reviewing scholarly research, forming research questions, designing a study, collecting and analyzing data, and sharing findings. Develops skills in the critical consumption of research. Course overlaps with: TSOCWF 390 and SOC WF 390. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 2.0 in either QMETH 201, STAT 220, STAT 221/CS&SS 221/SOC 221, STAT 311, TSOCWF 351, TMATH 110, or T URB 225.

records.title: Criminal Courts and Society
records.header: T CRIM 395 Criminal Courts and Society (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 395 Criminal Courts and Society (5) SSc Examines the background, legal principles, and structures of criminal courts in the United States. Explores the roles of court actors, procedures, and practices which uphold or threaten basic rights and liberties. Focuses on contemporary issues, including the development of alternative and specialized courts. Utilizes a critical, social justice lens to examine criminal courts and their impacts on society.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Advanced Readings in Criminal Justice
records.header: T CRIM 409 Advanced Readings in Criminal Justice (1-5, max. 15)
records.text: T CRIM 409 Advanced Readings in Criminal Justice (1-5, max. 15) Student-initiated, individually contracted course of study targeted at developing greater mastery of a specific area within criminal justice under the supervision of a social work faculty member with expertise in a related area of criminal justice. Focuses on individualized student-centered learning with emphasis on achievement of stated student learning objectives.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Racialized Disproportionality Across Systems
records.header: T CRIM 427 Racialized Disproportionality Across Systems (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 427 Racialized Disproportionality Across Systems (5) SSc Examines disproportionate representation of people of color in the child welfare, economic, education, health, juvenile justice, and mental health systems. Focuses on how each of these systems interacts with criminal legal systems in which racialized disproportionality is a particularly serious problem. Course overlaps with: T EDUC 490. Offered: jointly with TSOCWF 427.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Children of Incarcerated Parents
records.header: T CRIM 430 Children of Incarcerated Parents (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 430 Children of Incarcerated Parents (5) SSc Examines the impact of parental incarceration on the psychological, social, physical, and biological development of children. Focuses on issues of loss, trauma, attachment, and ways to address such issues. Offered: jointly with TSOCWF 430.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Trauma-Informed Interventions with Systems-Impacted People
records.header: T CRIM 433 Trauma-Informed Interventions with Systems-Impacted People (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 433 Trauma-Informed Interventions with Systems-Impacted People (5) SSc Provides an overview of trauma theory and pathways to trauma transformation. Explores the role of trauma in harm-doing, victimization, and the practices of criminal legal systems. Teaches effective interventions and skills for working with and supporting healing among those who cause harm and those who experience harm as victims. Offered: jointly with TSOCWF 433.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Criminal Homicide
records.header: T CRIM 434 Criminal Homicide (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 434 Criminal Homicide (5) SSc Examines the causes, forms, and consequences of homicide offending and victimization. Explores the patterns and characteristics of various forms of homicide. Analyzes the effectiveness of solutions and interventions both within and beyond criminal legal systems. Course overlaps with: SOC 275.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Terrorism, Crime, and Justice
records.header: T CRIM 435 Terrorism, Crime, and Justice (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 435 Terrorism, Crime, and Justice (5) SSc Explores terrorism and counterterrorism organizations from a criminological perspective. Traces the evolution of domestic and international terrorism organizations and networks within the United States and globally, including motivations and tactics, and the counterterrorism strategies used by law enforcement. Analyzes the social construction of terrorism in academic and popular discourses.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Contemporary Social Work in Criminal Justice Settings
records.header: T CRIM 436 Contemporary Social Work in Criminal Justice Settings (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 436 Contemporary Social Work in Criminal Justice Settings (5) SSc Focuses on social work practice with justice-involved individuals in criminal justice settings including juvenile justice, specialty courts, community corrections, jail and prison. Describes social work roles at multiple levels and examines contemporary issues that impact social work practice. Explores promising social work interventions and what is needed for effective practice. Offered: jointly with TSOCWF 436.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Abolitionism and Revolutionary Criminology
records.header: T CRIM 437 Abolitionism and Revolutionary Criminology (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 437 Abolitionism and Revolutionary Criminology (5) SSc Examines meanings of abolitionism and debates over dismantling the prison industrial complex. Compares criminal justice reforms to more revolutionary transformation of systems. Explores the liberating potential of abolitionist solutions to problems of crime, oppression, and injustice. Imagines transformative alternatives to build humane systems that address harms in the collective interest.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Fundamentals of Criminal Law
records.header: T CRIM 440 Fundamentals of Criminal Law (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 440 Fundamentals of Criminal Law (5) SSc Examines the historical, constitutional, and legal principles applicable to substantive criminal law. Analyzes the definition of criminal law, elements of major crimes, general principles of criminal responsibility, punishment, and the conditions that may excuse an individual from criminal liability or mitigate punishment.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Senior Seminar: Professionalism and Ethical Issues in Criminal Justice
records.header: T CRIM 441 Senior Seminar: Professionalism and Ethical Issues in Criminal Justice (5) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 441 Senior Seminar: Professionalism and Ethical Issues in Criminal Justice (5) SSc Examines the interaction between ethics and criminal justice practice, including application of ethical theory to criminal justice issues. Topics include ethical response to police brutality and corruption in criminal justice systems, development of professional identity, and promotion of professional conduct. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 2.0 in T CRIM 371; and a minimum grade of 2.0 in TSOCWF 390 or T CRIM 390.

records.title: Comparative Criminal Justice Systems
records.header: T CRIM 450 Comparative Criminal Justice Systems (1-15, max. 15) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 450 Comparative Criminal Justice Systems (1-15, max. 15) SSc Examines the design, function, and legal basis for non-United States criminal justice systems. Engages cross-cultural analyses of the connection between government, political, demographic, and economic factors in explaining historical and contemporary trends. Compares and contrasts non-United States and United States criminal justice systems. Includes a study abroad component.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Independent Research in Criminal Justice
records.header: T CRIM 490 Independent Research in Criminal Justice (1-3, max. 12)
records.text: T CRIM 490 Independent Research in Criminal Justice (1-3, max. 12) Student-initiated, individually contracted research with a faculty member to engage the design and implementation of original empirical research. Training and supervision in some or all aspects of criminological/criminal justice research. Active participation as member of research team, with emphasis on achievement of state student learning objectives.
records.schedulingNote: Catalog prerequisites/offering patterns are not current registration permission or guaranteed future offerings.

records.title: Criminology and Justice Studies Internship
records.header: T CRIM 498 Criminology and Justice Studies Internship (5-15, max. 15) SSc
records.text: T CRIM 498 Criminology and Justice Studies Internship (5-15, max. 15) SSc Engages in experiential learning by applying academic knowledge to justice-related professions. Develops professional competencies through working empathetically and effectively with crime- and systems-impacted individuals, families, and communities and/or engaging in policy, administrative, and advocacy work common to justice-related agencies. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 2.0 in either T CRIM 361/TSOCWF 361, T CRIM 365, or T CRIM 371. Credit/no-credit only.
